messages.subject: Error in permute vertices
parts:
Hi all,
I am experimenting with some simple IPMs in Nimble and my first instance I have adapted the code from CH.11 of Bayesian Population Analysis using WinBUGS and am running into a problem when creating the model.

Error code is:
Defining model Error in permute.vertices(graph, oldGraphID_2_newGraphID) : At topology.c:2795 : Permute vertices: invalid permutation vector size, Invalid value In addition: Warning message: In topological.sort(graph, mode = "out") : At structural_properties.c:3464 :graph contains a cycle, partial result is returned

I am not entirely sure what it is telling me is wrong - having searched across various other discussions in this group I think it may be something to do with dynamic indexing and I may need to construct a Nimble function but Im not really sure?

Code I am using is below, any help or advice on what to try would be very gratefully received!

Cheers
Dave

            } #j

messages.subject: Re: Error in permute vertices
parts: Dave, the error is coming from the cyclic dependence between elements of m[] and r[], in the following code (I've combined the two for-loops into a single loop, for clarity):

# Multinomial likelihood
    for (t in 1:(2 * (nyears - 1))){
        m[t, 1:nyears] ~ dmulti(pr[t, 1:10], r[t])
    # Calculate the number of released individuals

Here, m[t, 1:nyears] depends on r[t].
And r[t] is calculated as the sum of m[t, 1:10]
This creates a cycle in the graph (r depends on m, m depends on r), which is not allowed in model code.  The code must represent a directed acyclic graph.

Right now I won't posit other modelling approaches, but hopefully others on the list might chime in with some ideas, for this multinomial observation / multinomial number of trials cyclic problem.

Daniel

J <- c(64, 132,  86, 154, 156, 134, 116, 106, 110)

# 11.3.2. Analysis of the model
# Specify model in BUGS language
code <- nimbleCode({
      #-------------------------------------------------
      #  Integrated population model
      #  - Age structured model with 2 age classes:
      #        1-year old and adult (at least 2 years old)
      #  - Age at first breeding = 1 year
      #  - Prebreeding census, female-based
      #  - All vital rates assumed to be constant
      #-------------------------------------------------
     
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # 1. Define the priors for the parameters
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # Observation error
      tauy <- pow(sigma.y, -2)
      sigma.y ~ dunif(0, 50)
      #sigma2.y <- pow(sigma.y, 2)
     
      # Initial population sizes
      N1[1] ~ dnorm(100, 0.0001)     # 1-year
      Nad[1] ~ dnorm(100, 0.0001)    # Adults
     
      constraint_N1 ~ dconstraint(N1[1] >= 0)
      constraint_Nad ~ dconstraint(Nad[1] >= 0)
     
      # Survival and recapture probabilities, as well as productivity
      for (t in 1:(nyears - 1)){
         sjuv[t] <- mean.sjuv
         sad[t] <- mean.sad
         p[t] <- mean.p
         f[t] <- mean.fec
         }
     
      mean.sjuv ~ dunif(0, 1)
      mean.sad ~ dunif(0, 1)
      mean.p ~ dunif(0, 1)
      mean.fec ~ dunif(0, 20)
     
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # 2. Derived parameters
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # Population growth rate
      for (t in 1:(nyears - 1)){
         lambda[t] <- Ntot[t + 1] / Ntot[t]
         }
     
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # 3. The likelihoods of the single data sets
      #-------------------------------------------------
      # 3.1. Likelihood for population population count data (state-space model)
         # 3.1.1 System process
         for (t in 2:nyears){
            mean1[t] <- f[t - 1] / 2 * sjuv[t - 1] * Ntot[t - 1]
            N1[t] ~ dpois(mean1[t])
            Nad[t] ~ dbin(sad[t - 1], Ntot[t - 1])
            }
         for (t in 1:nyears){
            Ntot[t] <- Nad[t] + N1[t]
            }
         
         # 3.1.2 Observation process
         for (t in 1:nyears){
            y[t] ~ dnorm(Ntot[t], tauy)
            }
     
      # 3.2 Likelihood for capture-recapture data: CJS model (2 age classes)
      # Multinomial likelihood
      for (t in 1:(2 * (nyears - 1))){
         m[t, 1:nyears] ~ dmulti(pr[t, 1:10], r[t])
         }
     
      # Calculate the number of released individuals
      for (t in 1:(2 * (nyears - 1))){
         r[t] <- sum(m[t, 1:10])
         }
     
      # m-array cell probabilities for juveniles
      for (t in 1:(nyears - 1)){
         # Main diagonal
         q[t] <- 1 - p[t]
         pr[t, t] <- sjuv[t] * p[t]
         
         # Above main diagonal
         for (j in (t + 1):(nyears - 1)){
            pr[t, j] <- sjuv[t] * prod(sad[(t + 1):j]) * prod(q[t:(j - 1)]) * p[j]
            } #j    
   
         # Below main diagonal
         for (j in 1:(t - 1)){
            pr[t, j] <- 0
            } #j
         
         # Last column: probability of non-recapture
         pr[t, nyears] <- 1 - sum(pr[t, 1:(nyears - 1)])
         } #t
     
      # m-array cell probabilities for adults
      for (t in 1:(nyears - 1)){
         # Main diagonal
         pr[t + nyears - 1, t] <- sad[t] * p[t]
         
         # Above main diagonal
         for (j in (t + 1):(nyears - 1)){
            pr[t + nyears - 1, j] <- prod(sad[t:j]) * prod(q[t:(j - 1)]) * p[j]
            } #j

         # Below main diagonal
         for (j in 1:(t - 1)){
            pr[t + nyears - 1, j] <- 0
            } #j
         
         # Last column
         pr[t + nyears - 1, nyears] <- 1 - sum(pr[t + nyears - 1, 1:(nyears - 1)])
         } #t
     
      # 3.3. Likelihood for productivity data: Poisson regression
      for (t in 1:(nyears - 1)){
         J[t] ~ dpois(rho[t])
         rho[t] <- R[t] * f[t]
         }
}
)

# Bundle data
nyears = 10
consts = list(nyears = nyears)
data = list(constraint_Nad = 1, constraint_N1 = 1, m = m, J = J, R = R)

# Initial values
inits <- list(mean.sjuv = runif(1, 0, 1), mean.sad = runif(1, 0, 1), mean.p = runif(1, 0, 1), mean.fec = runif(1, 0, 10),
              N1 = rpois(dim(m)[2], 30), Nad = rpois(dim(m)[2], 30), sigma.y = runif(1 ,0, 10))


model <- nimbleModel(code = code, constants = consts, data = data, inits = inits)
